newsitem.title: INDIA: Financial institutions push Delhi shares higher.
newsitem.headline: Financial institutions push Delhi shares higher.

text.p: Shares on the Delhi Stock Exchange built on early gains and closed higher on broad-based buying by foreign and domestic financial institutions, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index ended up 5.28 points at 743.25.
"The rise in share prices was expected as the slight decline in the prices on Friday was merely a technical correction," said Param Hans of brokers Jade Investments.
Brokers said a loosening of monetary policy by the central bank earlier this month continued to fuel purchases.

On October 19, the Reserve Bank of India, as part of the monetary policy for the second half of the year 1996/97 (April-March), announced a two-percentage point cut in the cash reserve ratio of banks to 10 percent, effective in four stages over the next four months.
Hindustan Lever rose 7.00 rupees to 816.50 on institutional buying.
Reliance Industries closed 0.20 rupee higher at 212.20, after touching an early high of 216 rupees, brokers said.
State Bank of India rose 0.50 rupee to 232.25, while Apollo tyres shot up 8.00 rupees to 128.25 on heavy buying by speculators, brokers said.
ITC edged up 0.75 rupees to 315.75 and Nestle jumped 10.95 rupees to 228.05.
